name: Puzzle game
summary: A family of grid/board games where the player manipulates tiles or pieces to reach a win condition. Subtypes differ a lot: match-3, jigsaw, sliding tiles, sokoban, hidden-object and logic grids.
entities: board or grid (rows, columns, cell size)
tiles/pieces with type, position and state
move counter, timer, score and target
level definition (grid, goal, move limit, hints)
mechanics: Match-3: swap adjacent tiles, match 3+ of a kind, remove them, apply gravity, refill and resolve cascades.
Sliding puzzle: one empty cell, tiles slide into it; win when the arrangement matches the target.
Jigsaw: drag/rotate pieces into a target layout; snap when close enough.
Sokoban: push boxes onto targets; player cannot pull and cannot move through walls.
Hidden object: find listed objects in a scene; click accuracy and hint budget matter.
Logic grids (sudoku/nonogram): validate rows, columns and regions after every input.
Most puzzles need a no-moves/shuffle rule, a hint rule and a restart rule.
ux: Pointer and touch input; large hit areas on mobile.
Animate swap/match/fall but block input until the cascade settles.
Show moves/score/time, hint button, restart, level select and best score.
Persist progress locally; show a clear win/lose overlay with retry.
pitfalls: Generating a board with no possible moves (or an immediate accidental match).
Infinite cascades or score inflation; not capping chain resolution.
Accepting input during animation; double-counting a match.
Confusing row/column indices; off-by-one grid mapping.
Unlicensed art/audio; huge images that break mobile memory.
Difficulty spikes with no level tuning; hints that reveal nothing.
defaults: 6x6 match-3 grid, swap adjacent tiles, 3+ match, gravity and refill, 20 moves.
No timer, score target, hint after 10 seconds of inactivity, restart button.
5 hand-tuned levels, local progress, cat-themed tile art if the user asked for cats.

ask.en: Which puzzle mechanic should the game use?

suffix.en: Use a match-3 grid: swap adjacent tiles, match 3 or more, gravity and refill.
suffix.tr: 3'lü eşleştirme kullan: komşu taşları değiştir, 3+ eşleştir, yerçekimi ve yenileme uygula.

suffix.en: Use a jigsaw: drag pieces into the target layout and snap them into place.
suffix.tr: Yapboz kullan: parçaları hedef düzene sürükle ve yerine oturt.

suffix.en: Use a sliding-tile puzzle with one empty cell and a target arrangement.
suffix.tr: Tek boşluklu kayan taş puzzle'ı ve hedef dizilim kullan.

ask.en: How large should the first version be?
ask.tr: İlk sürüm ne kadar kapsamlı olsun?

suffix.en: Build one polished level with score, moves, hint and restart.
suffix.tr: Skor, hamle, ipucu ve yeniden başlatma içeren tek cilalı seviye yap.

suffix.en: Build five levels with increasing difficulty, level select and saved progress.
suffix.tr: Artan zorlukta beş seviye, seviye seçimi ve kayıtlı ilerleme yap.

ask.en: What visual theme should the tiles use?

suffix.en: Use cat illustrations for the tiles.
Use simple colored shapes for the tiles.
suffix.tr: Taşlar için basit renkli şekiller kullan.

verification: Initial board is solvable and has no unintended immediate matches.
Only adjacent swaps are accepted; a swap that creates no match is reverted.
A 3+ match removes the tiles, scores, applies gravity/refill and resolves cascades.
When no moves remain, the board shuffles or the level ends; it never freezes.
Win/lose conditions trigger once and show the correct overlay; restart resets board, moves and score.
Hint points to a real valid move; input is ignored during animations.
Touch and mouse input both work; progress persists after reload when requested.
